userStories.title: Add flush timer to worker handleData() for sub-second terminal output
userStories.description:
The worker's handleData() in backend/src/worker.ts buffers subprocess stdout into a `pending` buffer and only writes to the `run_output_chunks` DB table when `pending.length >= CHUNK_SIZE` (4096 bytes). With sparse initial execution-engine output (LLM thinking, tool warm-up), the first visible terminal output takes 45-60 seconds to appear.

Add a 500ms flush timer that writes whatever is in `pending` to the DB regardless of size. The timer must:
1. Start/restart on each `handleData()` call (debounce pattern — 500ms after last data arrival)
2. Be cleared when the size-based flush fires (coalesce — don't double-write the same bytes)
3. Be cleared and force-flush remaining bytes when the child process exits (existing `close`/`exit` handler)
4. Use `setInterval` or `setTimeout` — NOT `setImmediate` (too aggressive, would write every byte individually)
5. Keep the existing 4KB size-based flush for throughput during heavy output bursts (compilation output, large diffs)

The fix is localized to the `handleData()` function and the process exit cleanup in worker.ts. The `writeChunk()` helper that inserts into `run_output_chunks` already exists and handles sequence numbering.
acceptanceCriteria: A flush timer (500ms default) is added to handleData() that writes pending buffer contents to run_output_chunks regardless of buffer size
The timer is reset on each handleData() call so rapid data arrivals coalesce into a single write
When the size-based flush (4KB) fires, the timer is cleared to prevent double-writing the same data
When the child process exits, the timer is cleared and any remaining pending bytes are flushed immediately
The CHUNK_SIZE constant (4096) and size-based flush path remain unchanged for high-throughput scenarios

userStories.title: Jest tests for worker singleton guard and heartbeat-aware orphan sweep
userStories.description:
Write Jest tests for the worker singleton guard, heartbeat-aware stale job recovery, and heartbeat-aware orphan sweep that were previously added to `worker.ts`. These mechanisms prevent multiple worker instances from competing for the same pg-boss queue and prevent the orphan sweep from killing legitimate engine processes.

Create `backend/src/__tests__/worker-singleton-sweep.test.ts` with test cases:

**Singleton Guard:**
1. First worker instance acquires the singleton lock (INSERT into worker_heartbeat succeeds)
2. Second worker instance detects existing live heartbeat (last_seen < 90s ago) and exits with error
3. Second worker instance detects stale heartbeat (last_seen > 90s ago) and takes over the lock

**Heartbeat-Aware Stale Job Recovery (recoverStaleJobs):**
4. Jobs with `state='active'` AND no matching live worker heartbeat are marked failed
5. Jobs with `state='active'` AND a matching live worker heartbeat are left alone (legitimate in-progress work)
6. Recovery uses correct pg-boss column name `started_on` (NOT `startedon`)

**Heartbeat-Aware Orphan Sweep:**
7. Orphan sweep only kills processes whose worker_id has a stale heartbeat (last_seen > 90s)
8. Orphan sweep does NOT kill processes belonging to a live worker (last_seen < 90s)

Mock the database layer (pg Pool) and pg-boss instance. Test the SQL queries directly where possible.
acceptanceCriteria: Test file backend/src/__tests__/worker-singleton-sweep.test.ts exists with at least 8 test cases covering singleton guard, stale recovery, and orphan sweep
Singleton guard tests verify: first worker acquires lock, second worker with live heartbeat is rejected, second worker with stale heartbeat takes over
Stale job recovery tests verify: active jobs with dead workers are failed, active jobs with live workers are preserved
Orphan sweep tests verify: processes from stale workers are killed, processes from live workers are not killed
Tests verify correct pg-boss column names (started_on, completed_on) are used in queries
All tests pass when run with: npx jest --testPathPattern=worker-singleton-sweep

userStories.title: Extract handleData flush logic into testable FlushBuffer class
userStories.description:
The flush timer logic added in US-001 is embedded inside the worker's process spawning code, making it hard to unit test in isolation. Extract the buffering + flushing logic into a standalone `FlushBuffer` class in `backend/src/lib/flush-buffer.ts` that can be instantiated and tested independently.

The class should encapsulate:
- `pending: Buffer` — the accumulation buffer
- `CHUNK_SIZE: number` — configurable (default 4096)
- `FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS: number` — configurable (default 500)
- `onFlush: (data: Buffer) => Promise<void>` — callback invoked when flushing
- `write(data: Buffer): void` — append data, trigger size-based flush if threshold reached, reset/start timer
- `close(): Promise<void>` — flush remaining, clear timer
- Internal timer management (setTimeout/clearTimeout)

Then refactor worker.ts `handleData()` to use `new FlushBuffer({ chunkSize: 4096, flushInterval: 500, onFlush: writeChunk })` instead of inline buffer management. The behavioral contract must remain identical — this is a refactor, not a feature change.

Update the Jest tests from US-004 to test FlushBuffer directly (simpler, no worker mocking needed).

The behavioral contract is identical — no change in observable flushing behavior from US-001

userStories.title: Backend SSE endpoint injects story markers into output stream
userStories.description:
US-003 injects markers on the frontend by writing to the xterm instance. This works for live viewers but not for late-joiners who replay from `run_output_chunks`. Move the marker injection to the backend so markers are persisted in the DB and replayed correctly.

In `backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts`, the SSE endpoint `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/output` already streams chunks from `run_output_chunks`. Subscribe to WAL events (via sse-hub) for the current run. When a `story_passed`, `story_failed`, or `story_skipped` event arrives:
1. Format an ANSI-colored marker line (same format as US-003)
2. Write it to `run_output_chunks` as a new chunk with the next sequence number
3. The SSE stream will naturally pick it up and deliver it to all connected clients

This ensures:
- Live viewers see markers in real-time
- Late-joiners see markers during replay
- The marker is part of the persistent terminal history

The story title and elapsed time come from the WAL event payload. If the WAL event doesn't include the story title, look it up from `story_results` table.

After this is implemented, US-003's frontend-only injection becomes redundant but harmless (markers would appear twice). US-003 should be updated to check if the backend is already injecting markers and skip frontend injection to avoid duplicates — or simply remove the frontend injection entirely since backend injection is strictly superior.
acceptanceCriteria: The output SSE endpoint subscribes to WAL events for the current run and injects story completion markers into run_output_chunks
Markers use ANSI color codes: green for passed, red for failed, yellow for skipped
Markers are persisted in run_output_chunks with correct sequence numbers so late-joiners see them during replay
Each marker includes story ID, title, status, and elapsed time
No duplicate markers are written if the same WAL event is processed twice (idempotency guard)

userStories.title: Aggregate story pass counts across all runs in kanban endpoint
userStories.description: The `/api/specs/kanban` endpoint currently returns story pass/fail counts based only on the latest pipeline run for each spec. This means specs that required multiple runs to complete (e.g. run 121 passes US-001–US-003, run 122 resumes and passes US-004–US-009) show an incorrect progress bar — only the stories from the most recent run are counted. Fix the SQL query in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` to aggregate `story_results` across ALL runs for each spec using a DISTINCT ON (story_id) strategy that picks the best status (passed > failed > skipped) per story across all runs. A story counts as passed if it passed in ANY run for that spec.
acceptanceCriteria: The kanban endpoint aggregates story_results across all pipeline runs for a spec, not just the latest run_id, so a story that passed in run 121 still counts as passed when run 122 completes

The SQL uses a priority-based deduplication (passed > failed > skipped) per story_id so a story that passed in an earlier run is never downgraded to failed by a later run that re-attempted and failed it
A spec that completed across two runs (e.g. 3 stories in run 121 + 6 stories in run 122) shows all 9 stories as passed in the kanban progress bar
The fix does not break specs with only a single run — single-run pass counts remain identical to the previous behavior

A Jest test in `backend/src/__tests__/` covers the multi-run aggregation scenario: inserts story_results across two run_ids for the same spec and asserts the kanban response returns the correct aggregated passed/total counts

**Bug 1 — Terminal output 60-second delay (CRITICAL)**
The worker's `handleData()` in `backend/src/worker.ts` (lines 639-651) buffers subprocess stdout until 4KB accumulates before writing to `run_output_chunks` DB table. With sparse initial execution-engine output (LLM thinking, tool warm-up), the first visible output takes 45-60 seconds to appear. The `CHUNK_SIZE` is 4096 bytes and `pending` buffer only flushes when `pending.length >= CHUNK_SIZE`.

The Run View's stories tab uses a legacy `StoriesListTab` function (RunViewPanel.tsx lines 165-364) — a static list with dots and text, no live timers, no running indicator, no animations, no real-time WAL event updates. Additionally, the Terminal tab is the default, so even after Bug 2 is fixed, users watching the terminal miss story completions.

Fix: After wiring RunStoryList (Bug 2 fix), also inject per-story completion markers into the terminal stream. When a `story_passed` or `story_failed` WAL event arrives, inject a visible marker line into the xterm terminal (e.g. green `✓ US-001: Story Title — passed (elapsed)` or red `✗ US-002: Story Title — failed`). This gives terminal-watchers immediate feedback without switching tabs.

**Bug 4 — Worker singleton guard (already fixed, needs tests)**
Multiple worker instances were competing for the same pg-boss queue, causing orphan sweep to kill legitimate engine processes mid-story. A singleton guard, heartbeat-aware stale job recovery, and heartbeat-aware orphan sweep were added to `worker.ts`. These fixes need robust Jest tests.
